title: An Adiabatic Process is a Process in which No Energy as Heat is Transferred
lead: An ideal gas can expand reversibly at constant temperature, or with no heat let in at all. Following both routes between the same two states shows where the energy for the work comes from in each.
notes: Four of the book's equations are images that no longer load at the source; the lines in their place are reconstructed and footnoted.
exercise_notes: The book sets no exercises for this section; the one exercise, on the heat and work of a reversible isothermal doubling of volume, was written by AI with an AI solution, and its Bloom level and concept tags were chosen by AI. Numeric answers accept a 2% tolerance.

exercises.prompt: 1.00 mol of an ideal gas at 298 K doubles its volume in a reversible isothermal expansion. Find (a) the heat taken in and (b) the work done on the gas.

parts.hint: $\Delta U = 0$ for an isothermal change of an ideal gas, so $q_{rev} = nRT\ln(V_2/V_1)$.

answer.solution: The energy of an ideal gas depends only on its temperature, so $\Delta U = 0$ and $w_{rev} = -q_{rev}$. (a) $q_{rev} = nRT\ln(V_2/V_1) = (1.00\ \text{mol})(8.314\ \text{J K}^{-1}\text{mol}^{-1})(298\ \text{K})\ln 2 = +1717$ J, or +1.72 kJ. (b) $w_{rev} = -1.72$ kJ: the gas does 1.72 kJ of work on its surroundings, all of it paid for by the heat taken in.
